key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: While energy price inflation declined in June, its rise since the start of the conflict – and its impact on food, goods and services price inflation – is likely to keep inflation well above target into the first half of 2027.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Overall financial conditions have become slightly tighter since our previous meeting, consistent with the increase in the key ECB interest rates.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Remember how fast energy prices went down after the announcement of the Memorandum of Understanding.

briefing:
The ECB kept its key interest rates unchanged. The Hawk & Dove stance index rates the press conference as neutral: it ranks at the 56th percentile of the 54 press conferences held since December 2019, down from the 77th percentile at the previous meeting on 11 June 2026. The monetary policy statement ranks at the 63rd percentile and the answers in the Q&A at the 46th.

The ECB expects economic growth to remain modest in the near term, weighed down by the energy shock and related uncertainties [1]. The ECB's wage tracker and surveys on wage expectations continue to indicate moderate wage growth over the coming quarters [2]. The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside, with renewed disruption of energy supplies, a worsening of global financial market sentiment, or a tighter supply of credit potentially dampening demand [3].

The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside, with the energy shock potentially intensifying further and its effects on other prices and wages being stronger than currently expected [4]. The ECB will balance the agility of the Central Bank with avoiding sudden shifts in direction, taking into account the uncertainty and volatility of the current situation [5].
